section: Quit India Movement 1942 - causes, course, underground activity, repression, significance
subsections: Quit India in Andhra - Tenali, Bhimavaram, Kakinada

accepted.s: The Kurnool (Andhra) Circular, issued on 29 July 1942 during the Quit India Movement, was drafted by whom?
accepted.x: The Kurnool (Andhra) Circular was drafted by Kala Venkat Rao on 29 July 1942. It was subsequently seized by the police at Kurnool.
accepted.tq: Use the author–document trap by distinguishing the drafter from other Andhra leaders.
accepted.sec: Quit India in Andhra - Tenali, Bhimavaram, Kakinada

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee met at Machilipatnam during the Quit India Movement under the leadership of
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee met at Machilipatnam under Pattabhi Sitaramayya during the Quit India Movement.
accepted.tq: Test the venue–leader association directly, a common place-and-person trap.
accepted.sec: Quit India in Andhra - Tenali, Bhimavaram, Kakinada

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Place)
a. Tenali
b. Guntur
c. Bhimavaram
d. Kakinada

List-II (Incident)
i. Lawyers passed a resolution demanding Gandhi’s release
ii. Police firing on 13 August 1942
iii. Police firing on 12 August 1942 and burning of the Madras–Puri passenger train
iv. Firing on 17 August 1942 and attack on the Collectorate

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Tenali witnessed firing on 12 August and the burning of the Madras–Puri passenger train; Guntur witnessed firing on 13 August; Bhimavaram witnessed firing on 17 August and an attack on the Collectorate; and Kakinada lawyers demanded Gandhi’s release.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure place–incident pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped event.
accepted.sec: Quit India in Andhra - Tenali, Bhimavaram, Kakinada

accepted.s: During the Quit India Movement in Andhra, which one of the following places was associated with the cutting of signal wires and the burning of a post office?
accepted.x: Signal wires were cut at Chirala, while a post office was burnt at Tadepalligudem.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely associated places by matching each location with its specific act.
accepted.sec: Quit India in Andhra - Tenali, Bhimavaram, Kakinada

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra University during the Quit India Movement:
1. A resolution was adopted under Mamidipudi Venkatrangayya.
2. Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool remained underground throughout the movement.
3. The resolution was adopted under the leadership of Tanguturi Prakasam.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Andhra University resolution was under Mamidipudi Venkatrangayya, while Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool remained underground throughout; Tanguturi Prakasam was not stated as the leader of this resolution.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped-person statement by separating the university resolution from the underground activity.
accepted.sec: Quit India in Andhra - Tenali, Bhimavaram, Kakinada

accepted.s: A collective fine of Rs 6,000 was imposed during the Quit India Movement on which place in Andhra?
accepted.x: Akividu in West Godavari was subjected to a collective fine of Rs 6,000.
accepted.tq: Link the exact monetary figure with its location rather than with another Andhra centre of agitation.
accepted.sec: Quit India in Andhra - Tenali, Bhimavaram, Kakinada

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding punitive measures during the Quit India Movement in Andhra is correct?
o: Grain belonging to N.G. Ranga was seized at Nidudavolu.
A collective fine of Rs 6,000 was imposed at Nidudavolu.
Grain belonging to N.G. Ranga was seized at Akividu.
The grain seizure was imposed on Kakinada lawyers.
accepted.x: The grain of N.G. Ranga was seized at Nidudavolu. Akividu, in West Godavari, was separately subjected to a collective fine of Rs 6,000.
accepted.tq: Separate the place associated with a fine from the place associated with seizure of grain.
accepted.sec: Quit India in Andhra - Tenali, Bhimavaram, Kakinada

accepted.s:
In the imposition of collective fines in Andhra during the Quit India Movement, which of the following groups were exempted?
1. Muslims
2. Christians
3. Scheduled Castes
4. Government employees

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Muslims, Christians, Scheduled Castes and government employees were exempted from the collective fines.
accepted.tq: Check the complete composition of the exempted groups before choosing the inclusive code.
accepted.sec: Quit India in Andhra - Tenali, Bhimavaram, Kakinada

accepted.s: The underground paper circulated in Andhra during the Quit India Movement carried which of the following messages?
o: Vande Mataram and Do or Die
accepted.x: The underground paper titled “Quit India” circulated the message “Rahasya Udyamam Saginchandi.”
accepted.tq: Test the exact wording of an underground publication instead of substituting a famous national slogan.
accepted.sec: Quit India in Andhra - Tenali, Bhimavaram, Kakinada

accepted.s: Why did the Communist Party of India oppose the Quit India Movement in 1942?
o: It considered the movement an exclusively provincial movement in Andhra.
It supported the Muslim League’s demand for Pakistan from the beginning of the war.
It supported the British war effort after Nazi Germany attacked the Soviet Union.
It had already withdrawn from Indian politics after the Civil Disobedience Movement.
accepted.x: The Communists opposed the Quit India Movement because, after the Nazi attack on the Soviet Union, they backed the British war effort.
accepted.tq: Identify the cause–attitude link rather than confusing Communist policy with the position of the Muslim League.

accepted.s: The ban on the Communist Party of India was lifted on
accepted.x: The ban on the Communist Party of India was lifted on 23 July 1942.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the CPI ban-lifting date from the dates of the Quit India resolution and Andhra incidents.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Communist Party of India after its policy during the Quit India period?
o: It did not contest the elections of 1945–46 owing to the continuation of its ban.
It formed the provincial government in Andhra after the elections of 1945–46.
It won heavily in the elections of 1945–46 because of its support for the movement.
It lost heavily in the elections of 1945–46 after opposing the Quit India Movement.
accepted.x: The Communist Party of India lost heavily in the 1945–46 elections. Its opposition to the Quit India Movement and support for the British war effort formed the background to its political position during this period.
accepted.tq: Use the electoral outcome as a chronological consequence of the party’s wartime policy.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the attitude of political groups and communities towards the Quit India Movement:
1. The Muslim League stayed away from the movement.
2. The Hindu Mahasabha stayed away from the movement.
3. The princely states stayed away from the movement.
4. Muslims generally sheltered activists, and communal clashes did not occur.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Muslim League, Hindu Mahasabha and princely states stayed away, while Muslims generally sheltered activists and there were no communal clashes.
accepted.tq: Test several parallel attitudes together, including the less obvious community-level response.

accepted.s: Which one of the following best expresses the significance of the Quit India Movement?
o: It secured immediate transfer of power before the end of the Second World War.
It was Gandhi’s first mass movement against British rule.
It was confined mainly to constitutional negotiations with the British Government.
It was Gandhi’s final mass movement and demonstrated that independence could not be postponed after the war.
accepted.x: The Quit India Movement was Gandhi’s final mass movement. It showed that Indian independence could not be postponed after the war.
accepted.tq: Choose the precise significance statement and reject claims of immediate independence or a merely constitutional campaign.

accepted.s: In the context of Andhra Pradesh, the Quit India Movement is described as the
o: last campaign led exclusively by the Communist Party in Andhra
first constitutional campaign of the freedom struggle in Andhra
final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra
movement that began the formation of Andhra Province
accepted.x: In the Andhra context, the Quit India Movement is regarded as the final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra. Tanguturi Prakasam emerged as a leading figure during this phase.
accepted.tq: Apply the regional significance phrase exactly and avoid replacing it with a broader constitutional description.

accepted.s: Who emerged as a leading figure in Andhra during the Quit India Movement?
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam emerged as a leading figure in Andhra during the Quit India Movement.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the prominent regional figure from leaders associated with particular documents or underground work.
